- When sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values.
- When sentiment is bearish (negative) or mixed, model often underestimates upside; increase forecast mid-range or late-period values.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting upward; accelerate upward correction after sentiment flip.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) values when sentiment is positive; add 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to ignore volatility; increase forecast variance (±0.5–1.0%) to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
